title: Minimum Suffix Flips
summary: Given a binary string target of length n, you start with a binary string s of the same length, initially filled with zeros.
statement: Given a binary string target of length n, you start with a binary string s of the same length, initially filled with zeros. You can perform an operation where you flip all the bits from any index i to the end of the string. The goal is to make string s match the target string. Determine the minimum number of such operations needed to achieve this.
constraints: Start with an all-zero string of target’s length.
A move flips every bit from one chosen index through the end; return the minimum moves to reach target.
hints: All positions at and after the latest flip share one current effective bit.
Scan target left to right; when its bit differs from that state, a flip is necessary.
Count the flip and update the effective bit.
Earlier positions can no longer be changed without breaking them, so every mismatch forces exactly one optimal flip.
editorial: Earlier positions can no longer be changed without breaking them, so every mismatch forces exactly one optimal flip.

tests.explanation: Transitions 0→1, 1→0, and 0→1 require three suffix flips.
The initial string already matches, so no flips are needed.
